title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, as best it can be inferred from pp. 611-616 of the manuscript. The page carries archive no. 615; its handwritten page number cannot be read with confidence. Ĝ^+ is evidently the profinite completion of PSL2(Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3, with generators σ (order 2) and ρ (order 3). Π^ is a normal free profinite subgroup of rank 2 with Ĝ^+/Π^ ≅ S_3 (Ĝ_3), presumably the image of Γ(2); Π_0 is its index-2 refinement. M is a group of automorphisms of Ĝ^+, a GT-like group. M(0) and M[0] = Z^!_{ρ,σ} are stabilizer-type subgroups attached to the two 'vertices' ρ and σ. N*_ρ and N*_σ are normalizer-type groups, and L_ρ, L_σ are the finite subgroups generated by ρ and σ. Γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ Γ̃_Q is the arithmetic quotient, written γ_{ρ,σ} on p. 611 and Π_φ~ on this page.

Problem being served. Grothendieck wants to split the extension (133) 1 → L_σ → N*_σ → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1 canonically, and to realise the section as an explicit subgroup.

Step 1. He rewrites (132) as Γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ M^!_0[0]/L_0^{Π_0}, where M^!_0[0] := M(0)·L_0^{Π_0} is an index-2 subgroup of M^![0] = M(0)·L_0^!.

Step 2. The natural map M^![0] = Z^!_{ρ,σ} → N*_σ is trivial on L_0^{Π_0}. It therefore factors through Γ_{ρ,σ}, which gives the splitting N*_σ ≅ Γ_{ρ,σ}·L_σ (semidirect product).

Step 3. He identifies the section subgroup inside G_{ρ,σ} ≅ M as (134), N^{!*}_{0σ} := Im(M_0[0] → N*) = Im(M[0] ↪ N*). Concretely it is the set of β^{-1}u with u ∈ M(0), β ∈ Π̂_0 and u(σ) = ε_2(u)·i_{-1}(β)~(σ). Equivalently it is the set of v ∈ N*_σ for which some β ∈ Π̂_0 gives βv ∈ M[0]. In other words, one corrects an element of the stabilizer M(0) by an inner automorphism from Π̂_0 so that it normalises the order-2 subgroup in the prescribed way, with a sign given by the quadratic character ε_2.

Step 4 (marginal NB). M^! is defined as the inverse image of M^!_{0,3} under the canonical representation M → Ĝ^+/Π^ ≅ Aut(·) ≅ S_3. Then (135) sets M^!_0 = M(0)·Π_0 ⊂ M^! = M(0)·Π, of index 2.

Outcome (next page). M^! ≅ M^!_0 × μ. The section group is renamed M(1/2), and one gets the semidirect decompositions M ≅ M(1/2)·Ŝ^+, M^! ≅ M(1/2)·Π̂ and N*_σ ≅ M(1/2)·L_σ. This is the analogue, for the 'σ-vertex', of the GT-type description of automorphism groups of profinite PSL2(Z) and free groups as split extensions of a Galois-type group by inner automorphisms.
errors: In (134) the image appears to read N*_ρ in the two 'Im' lines, while the final description and the surrounding text concern N*_σ. This is probably a slip of ρ for σ, or a correction in progress.

Grothendieck crossed out 'isomorphisme' and replaced it with 'scindage'. Some notational conflation between M_0[0], M^!_0[0] and M[0] remains; he asserts that the images coincide without justification.
The claim that the map Z^! → N*_σ is trivial on L_0^{Π_0} is stated without proof.

ideas.what: Canonical splitting of the extension of the arithmetic group Γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ Γ̃_Q by the finite stabilizer L_σ inside a normalizer, via the quotient M^!_0[0]/L_0^{Π_0}.
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of GT-type automorphism groups of profinite PSL2(Z) / cusp-elliptic point stabilizers.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (GT^, 1990); Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura; Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki (automorphisms of profinite PSL2(Z)-type groups).
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme appears, in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, GT-type group); this computation is unpublished.

ideas.what: Explicit description of the section subgroup as stabilizer elements corrected by inner automorphisms of Π̂_0 with a quadratic-character twist ε_2.
ideas.modern_name: Normalized lifts / 'β^{-1}u' correction (analogue of the f-component normalisation in GT^).

ideas.what: M^! as the inverse image of a subgroup under M → Ĝ^+/Π^ ≅ S_3, with index-2 subgroups M^!_0 = M(0)·Π_0.
ideas.modern_name: Level-2 (Γ(2)) structure / S_3 action on the cusps of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}.

missed.claim: The page shows Grothendieck systematically treating the GT-type group as a split extension of Γ̃_Q at each of the elliptic points (σ of order 2, ρ of order 3) of PSL2(Z). The sections are given explicitly with quadratic-character twists ε_2 and ε_3. This is in line with the later literature, but the explicit M(1/2) construction is unpublished.
missed.quote: Ainsi on a vu une scindage de (133) 1 → L_σ → N*_σ → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1 en un produit semi-direct
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest: it documents that Grothendieck worked out the PSL2(Ẑ)-elliptic-point version of the GT^ structure. Mathematically it seems to be subsumed by later work.

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful bookkeeping of semidirect product decompositions within an unpublished GT-type investigation. The structural results resemble known later results on automorphisms of profinite PSL2(Z) and GT^, and no clearly new idea is visible on this page.
transcription_corrections: (132) should read Γ_{ρ,σ} ≃ M^!_0[0]/L_0^{Π_0} (Γ, as in the transcription, rather than the γ of p. 611). The handwritten 'sous-groupe d'indice 2' annotation refers to M^!_0[0] ⊂ M^![0].
The handwritten 'M^![0] = M(0).L_0^!' is right, with superscript '!' on L_0.
In (134) the target in the Im lines appears to be N_ρ^* in the image (likely a slip for N_σ^*). The deleted symbol before ^{!*}_{0σ} is a crossed-out N, not M.
The condition in (134) reads 'u(σ) = ε_2(u) i_{-1}(β)~(σ)'.
The last line of (134) reads 'β v ∈ M[0] = Norm_{M^!}(L_0)' (a normaliser in M^!).
'qu'il vaut mieux écrire en contre-sens[?]' is likely 'qu'il vaut mieux écrire en considérant le sous-groupe de section en tant que sous-groupe de G_{ρ,σ} ≃ M'.
(135) is M^!_0 = M(0).Π_0 ⊂ M^! = M(0).Π (index 2), preceded by 'Posant dfn'.
The archive page number is 615 (bottom left); the handwritten page number is not legible with confidence.
